title: Allow documented PR recovery pair

sources.reason: The aggregate PR gate needs a narrowly auditable recovery-pair exception.
Regression evidence for accepted and rejected recovery relations.
Current finish evidence truncates output before the actionable failure tail.
Current quality graph runs expensive tests concurrently with later static gates.
Current pull-request smoke runs full quality before candidate release preflight.
Regression coverage for quality phase ordering and release gate ownership.
The user authorized continuous process correction and requires every process issue to be recorded.

riskAssessment.reason: The exception is deterministic and repository-local; all unrelated multi-Work-Item PRs remain rejected.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized the corrective path without further confirmation; tests and PR checks remain mandatory.

preReviewWarnings: Do not broaden the default one Work Item/one PR rule; accept only one source-linked, human-approved, sequential recovery pair.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: The aggregate PR gate accepts exactly one adjacent recovery pair only when predecessor source reference, human approval, Start Receipt, and Git ancestry all validate.
Ordinary multi-Work-Item PRs, missing predecessor references, unapproved recovery, and unrelated bases remain fail-closed.
Regression tests cover acceptance and rejection paths.
Static quality checks run before full pytest/coverage, and quality phases expose gate-specific exit evidence without hiding a cheap failure behind a long-running sibling.
Release distribution preflight runs before the expensive repository quality graph in pull-request smoke.
AI finish evidence preserves a failure tail and durable output digest metadata.
RFE-ISSUE-074 through RFE-ISSUE-079 record the recovery cycle, the quality failure, and the corrective process boundaries, including Make target-scanner compatibility and checkpoint refresh ordering.
guidelines: Preserve the one Work Item/one PR default and make exceptions deterministic and auditable.
Do not weaken immutable-tag or release-publication boundaries.

intent.problem: PR #401 requires a user-authorized candidate recovery after a Draft tag failure, but its two archived Work Items are rejected as a generic multi-Work-Item PR. The first standalone correction also exposed a second process defect: make quality waited behind a long pytest sibling while mypy failed, and ai-finish retained only the output prefix.
constraints: Deliver the gate and minimal quality/release orchestration correction in this standalone one-Work-Item PR.
Permit only one adjacent recovery pair.
Require source-linked predecessor, human approval, Start Receipt, and Git ancestry.
Do not publish or mutate release state.
Preserve all existing quality checks and supply-chain boundaries.
intent.rationale: A standalone PR preserves the default lifecycle; phased quality and durable failure evidence prevent another opaque long retry before #401 is resumed.

rawUserRequest: Continue without pausing; correct process problems first, record them, and do not weaken gates.

declaredIntent.summary: Add a narrow audited PR recovery-pair rule in its own normal Work Item PR.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: The user explicitly authorized continued corrective process work without another confirmation.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff and restore related tests and docs.
